questions.q: Where should you download Python from for use with Power BI?
options: The official python.org installer, not the Microsoft Store version
Only through Power BI Desktop's built-in installer
Any third-party Python distribution works identically
Python comes pre-installed with Power BI Desktop
questions.explain: Power BI runs scripts directly through python.exe from a folder you specify. The Microsoft Store's sandboxed install can cause path problems that break this connection — the official python.org installer avoids that.

questions.q: What is the one setup checkbox that prevents the most common installation problem?
questions.explain: Skipping 'Add python.exe to PATH' is the single most common reason a working Python install still can't be found later, whether by Power BI or by a terminal.

questions.q: Which two libraries does Power BI's Python integration specifically require?
questions.explain: Pandas makes data import possible at all (Power BI can only import a Pandas DataFrame), and Matplotlib powers the Python visual covered in Lesson 19.

questions.q: What command installs Pandas after Python itself is set up?
questions.explain: pip is Python's package installer, and 'pip install pandas' is the standard command to add the Pandas library — it ships with modern Python installers automatically.

questions.q: What does it mean if `python --version` returns an error in the terminal after installation?
options: The 'Add python.exe to PATH' checkbox was likely missed during setup, and Python should be reinstalled with it checked
Power BI Desktop needs to be reinstalled
This error is expected and can be ignored
questions.explain: A python --version error after installation almost always traces back to the PATH checkbox being skipped — the fix is reinstalling with that box checked, not working around the symptom.
